target.name: Matic Robotics
target.founder: Navneet Dalal, Mehul Nariyawala, Shafaq Presswala

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Matic Robotics is a seed-stage consumer technology company founded by Navneet Dalal, Mehul Nariyawala, and Shafaq Presswala. The company has raised $107M to date. No public comparables exist in the relevant sector, and the analysis is constrained by the absence of private peer transaction data.

Given limited comparative benchmarks, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised of $107M as a proxy baseline and normalizing to a $7M seed-stage equivalent value, application of a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $18M. This reflects the conventional step-up in company value between seed and Series A rounds in early-stage technology investing.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, with a median point estimate of $18M. The width of this range ($5M, or roughly 33% on either side of the median) reflects methodological constraints rather than fundamental uncertainty about the business. The primary limitation is reliance on a single method without corroborating evidence from comparable transactions or market multiples. A more robust valuation would require either access to private peer financing data or visibility into revenue and growth metrics to support revenue or growth-multiple approaches. Until such data becomes available, the stage-progression result should be treated as a preliminary indicator requiring validation through additional diligence.
